patch_description: The insight summary recommends iterating the local refinement: after the first `_local_shift_search` plateaus, re-run the grow/relax refinement (`_refine`) from the improved centers, then re-enter `_local_shift_search` with only the finest deltas. The rationale is that a single pass of greedy axis-aligned shifts leaves slack: once centers move, the water-filling radii distribution changes, and coordinated multi-circle relaxations (which `_refine` provides) can unlock further small shifts that were previously rejected. This shift→relax→shift fixed-point iteration monotonically improves (we always keep the best-scoring layout) and costs little time. I also extend `_local_shift_search` with diagonal moves (both axes shifted simultaneously), since many improving directions in hexagonal layouts are neither purely horizontal nor purely vertical, and add a finer final delta (0.0005).
